q: What are some of the strangest deep-sea creatures that we've only recently discovered?
What are the strangest deep-sea creatures?
What weird animals live in the deep ocean?
What are the most bizarre deep-sea creatures?
What creatures live in the deep ocean?
What are the strangest ocean animals?
a: The deep ocean, one of the least explored places on Earth, is home to some of the strangest and most bizarre creatures. The anglerfish uses a bioluminescent lure to attract prey in the dark depths. The gulper eel has an enormous mouth and elastic stomach that can swallow prey larger than itself. The barreleye fish has transparent, upward-facing eyes inside a transparent head that can rotate to spot silhouettes of prey above. The yeti crab lives around hydrothermal vents and farms bacteria on its hairy claws. The vampire squid survives in oxygen-poor waters by using a unique form of oxygen conservation and can invert its webbed arms to trap debris. The goblin shark has a protrusible jaw that shoots forward to catch prey. The giant isopod, a deep-sea relative of the pill bug, can grow to enormous sizes. The fangtooth fish has some of the largest teeth relative to body size of any fish. The dumbo octopus uses ear-like fins to 'fly' through the water. The yeti squid has rotating, squid-like arms and lacks a beak. Many of these creatures have evolved bioluminescence for communication, camouflage, and attracting prey in the perpetual darkness of the deep sea. New species are discovered regularly as deep-sea exploration technology advances.
